 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Satyavrat Verma
Oral Order
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned AC to SC-23 for the State and the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Railways.

2. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that vide Land Settlement Case No.IIT/1958-59,
land pertaining to Khata No.18, Khesra Nos.41, 44, 45, 46, 47 and 48, area 09 acre 37 decimals at Mauza- Bhelaguri, Block-Tedhagach, Thana No.125, District- Purnia now Kishanganj was settled with the Patna High Court CWJC No.546 of 2025(3) dt.07-04-2025 grandfather of the petitioner.
It is further submitted that thereafter, Jamabandi No.23 was created with respect to the land settled in favour of the grandfather of the petitioner in the Year 1959.

It is next submitted that since 1959, the ancestors of the petitioner and thereafter, petitioner is paying the rent of the land to the State of Abhay Kumar Singh vs The Union Of India on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179827814/
1 Bihar.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the rent of the land has been paid up-till 2024-2025.
It is next submitted that the Jamabandi No.23 with respect to the land in dispute was created in the Year 1959 and since then, is continuing, hence the Jamabandi is a long standing Jamabandi.

3. It is next submitted that for Araria Galgalia New B.G. Rail Line, the land of the petitioner pertaining to Khata No.18, Plot No.44, 45, 46 and 47 measuring an area 01 acre, 25 decimals, 400 square Kari was acquired vide Land Acquisition Case No.05 of 2019-2020.

entities.text: Araria Galgalia New B.G. Rail Line
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The learned counsel next submits that the notification by which the aforesaid land was acquired for the aforesaid rail project recorded the name of the State of Bihar as the owner of the said land when the land belonged to the petitioner.

It is further submitted that what is not in dispute rather stands admitted is that the entire land in dispute was settled with the grandfather of the petitioner vide Settlement Case No.IIT/1958-59 and the Jamabandi created with respect to Patna High Court CWJC No.546 of 2025(3) dt.07-04-2025 the land in the Year 1959 was in existence in the Year 2020, as such, it absolutely does not stand to reason that as to on what basis in the notification dated 10.06.2021 issued by the District Land Acquisition Officer (Annexure- P/4), the name of the State of Bihar was recorded with respect to the land in dispute.

It is next submitted that this petitioner had approached this Court earlier by filing CWJC No.14754 of 2023 for seeking compensation of the land acquired with respect to Plot No.45, 46, 47 pertaining to Khata No.18.
It is next submitted that the case was taken up on 28.03.2024 and the Railways as well as respondent nos.4 to 6 were directed to file their respective counter-affidavit.

It is submitted that the State authorities instead of filing a counter-affidavit in compliance of the order dated 28.03.2024 in CWJC No.14754 of 2023, the Circle Officer, Tedhagachh recommended for cancelling the entire settlement made in favour of the grandfather of the petitioner in the Year 1958-1959 vide Land Settlement Case No.IIT/1958- 1959.

It is submitted that based on the recommendation of the Circle Officer, settlement cancellation case no.21 of 2024 was instituted in the Court of the Collector, Kishanganj and notices were issued upon the petitioner.

It is next submitted that the petitioner appeared and submitted his reply, but then,
the Patna High Court CWJC No.546 of 2025(3) dt.07-04-2025 Collector without appreciating the facts of the case in its correct perspective and without taking into consideration the reply filed by the petitioner passed an order dated 14.11.2024 cancelling the entire settlement made in favour of the ancestor of the petitioner with a direction to the Circle Officer to mutate the name of the State of Bihar over the entire land including the land which was acquired by the railways, which is impugned in the present writ petition.
4. The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the Collector acted in haste in cancelling the entire settlement of land made in favour of the ancestor of the petitioner without taking into consideration the stand/ reply filed by the petitioner in Settlement Cancellation Case No.21 of 2024.

It is further submitted that it absolutely does not stand to reason that when Plot Nos.44, 45, 46 and 47 were already acquired by the railways, then what jurisdiction the Collector had to decide the dispute with respect to the aforesaid plots which stood acquired for the reason that once an acquisition takes place, the land goes beyond the control of the authority and the owner.

It is also submitted that long standing Jamabandi cannot be cancelled in a summary proceeding and the law is well settled in that regard by this Court, but then, the Collector Patna High Court CWJC No.546 of 2025(3) dt.07-04-2025 being aware of the law proceeded to cancel the entire settlement and also directed the Circle Officer to mutate the name of the State of Bihar over the entire land Abhay Kumar Singh vs The Union Of India on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179827814/
2 including the acquired land.

sentences.text:
It is next submitted that if the name of the State of Bihar stands mutated in view of the order dated 14.11.2024 in Settlement Cancellation Case No.21 of 2024, then on what basis in the notification dated 10.06.2021, by which the aforesaid four plots were acquired,
the name of the State of Bihar was figuring as owner.
5. The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the State seeks four weeks' time for filing counter-affidavit.

6. Put up this case on 12.05.2025 at 10.30 A.M.
7.
The order dated 14.11.2024 in Settlement Cancellation Case No.21 of 2024 shall remain stayed until the writ application is finally adjudicated by this Court.
8. It is made clear that this order in no manner will affect the land which already stands acquired by the Railways for the aforesaid project.

(Satyavrat Verma, J) vikash/-
